usage.title: Usage
usage.text:
1. Add image, .spritefont, .wav or .mp3/.wma files with the toolbar or by dragging them into the list.
2. Choose the output directory at the top of the window.
3. Select an item to adjust texture or sprite font options on the right.
4. Click Build. Compiled .xnb files are written to the output directory.

Supported content (same as the original XNA Content Compiler):
- Textures: .bmp, .jpg, .png, .tga, .dds
- Sprite fonts: .spritefont
- Sound effects: .wav (PCM 8/16/24/32-bit or 32-bit float, mono/stereo)
- Songs: .mp3, .wma (the media file is copied next to the .xnb, like XNA Song content)

Options:
- Build > Graphics Profile switches between Reach (default) and HiDef. HiDef removes the power-of-two restriction from DXT compression and allows larger textures.
- Texture format can be Color (uncompressed), DXT compressed or No change, matching XNA's TextureProcessorOutputFormat.
- WAV loop points from the smpl chunk are preserved in the SoundEffect asset.
- DXT compression requires power-of-two texture dimensions in the Reach profile.

Notes:
- Output is XNA 4.0 (XNB version 5, Windows) and also loads in MonoGame and FNA.
- Content is written uncompressed: XNA's LZX compression is proprietary, and LZ4 output would not load in XNA 4.0.
- No XNA Game Studio, Visual Studio or .NET installation is required to run this tool.
about.title: About
about.description: Compile textures, sprite fonts, sound effects and songs into XNA 4.0 .xnb files without XNA Game Studio or Visual Studio.
about.components: Built with the MonoGame content pipeline, BCnEncoder.NET and Microsoft .NET.
cli.help:
XNA Content Compiler {0}

Usage:
  XnaContentCompiler.exe [project.xnccproj]
  XnaContentCompiler.exe --build <project.xnccproj> [--output <folder>] [--profile reach|hidef] [--lang en|zh]
  XnaContentCompiler.exe --help | --version

Options:
  --build, -b      Build the project without opening the UI.
  --output, -o     Override the project output directory.
  --profile        Graphics profile: reach (default) or hidef.
  --lang, -l       UI language: en, zh or auto.
  --help, -h       Show this help.
  --version        Show the version.
